title: UK CPI — September 2026 consumer price inflation (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the statutory uprating month, published seven days before the Autumn Budget
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukseptember2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release page reads 'Consumer price inflation, UK: September 2026', 'Release date: 21 October 2026 7:00am', and states 'This release is not yet published'. Primary-sourced (the publisher's own release calendar), filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap uk-cpi-2026-09-16 was filed under. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding TWO proposals read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md — proposals/uk-cpi-2026-10-21.from-boe-decision-2026-11-05.json and proposals/uk-cpi-2026-10-21.from-uk-cpi-2026-09-16.json. Both proposals' placement findings stand and are kept: this is the LAST CPI print before both the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget and the 2026-11-05 MPC meeting carrying the November Monetary Policy Report (the October-data bulletin publishes 2026-11-18, thirteen days after that vote), and it still does NOT contain the 1 October VAT zero-rating on domestic electricity (gov.uk, 21 July 2026, self-quantified at about -0.10pp on CPI). WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDED, AND ONE CORRECTION. (1) THE CORRECTION: the uk-cpi-2026-09-16 proposal's note that 'fuel duty rose 1p on 2026-09-01' is WRONG. gov.uk's 'Amended Fuel Duty rates: 2026 to 2027' (published 22 May 2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09) extends the temporary 5ppl cut to 31 December 2026 and supersedes the previous plan of 'reducing the cut by 1 ppl on 1 September 2026'; petrol and diesel stay at 0.5295/l, rising to 0.5595 on 2027-01-01 and 0.5795 on 2027-03-01. There is NO duty step in the September data. (2) THIS PRINT IS FISCALLY LOAD-BEARING IN A WAY NO OTHER MONTH'S IS. The September CPI figure is the statutory input to the following April's uprating: gov.uk's own business-rates letter 2/2026 (published 10 February 2026, fetched) quotes the formula in paragraph A10 of Schedule 7 to the Local Government Finance Act 1988 with 'C' = 'the consumer prices index for September 2025 = 139.3' against 'D' = September 2024 = 134.2, and the Social Security Benefits Up-rating Order 2026 (legislation.gov.uk, fetched) cites sections 150/150A/151/151A of the Social Security Administration Act 1992, the power under which benefits rose 3.8% in April 2026 — the September 2025 CPI rate exactly. So the 2026-10-21 number sets the 2027/28 business-rates multiplier and the April-2027 benefits and triple-lock prices leg, and it lands SEVEN DAYS BEFORE the Budget the OBR scores. (3) THE BASE MONTH IS A ZERO WITH AN EXCEPTIONAL COMPOSITION: ONS September 2025 bulletin (fetched) — 'CPI was unchanged in September 2025, as in September 2024', with air fares down 28.8% m/m ('the third-largest September decrease' since 2001) and live music down 8.6% m/m 'compared with a rise of 5.8% a year ago'. Against July 2026's much shallower summer air-fare spike (11.7% m/m vs 30.2% a year earlier), both one-offs have far less to repeat, which tilts the September 2026 monthly rate above zero and the annual rate up. Base case 3.0-3.4%, central ~3.2% — the Bank's own July-MPR Q4 peak — but stated WIDER than the sibling August print's 3.0-3.2% because this is a two-step chain: 2.9% plus TWO unknown monthly clears, not one. Tiered LOW and NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED: symbols: [], no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
